nodes.title: 01z PROMPT CONTROLS:  INSTR, STYLE, THEME
widgets_values:
:info: 01z (when enabled) is the LLM stage that takes the input prompt and attempt to extend it for the model you intend to use. I accepts prompt controls, in the form of `INSTR`, `STYLE`, and `THEME`. Add any of these to the input, and quote the string within: ``` THEME="medieval fantasy", STYLE="watercolor painting, loose washes", INSTR="replace the knights with a woman in a kimono", ``` `INSTR`: "Instructions" to ... edits the scene (replace, add, remove or change subjects, objects, actions, setting, camera or medium). Also handles whole-scene changes like "transform into a cyberpunk rendition".
`STYLE`: How the scene looks: medium, materials, surface texture, palette, lighting. It overrides conflicting style words in the scene but never changes who or what is in it.
`THEME`: The visual domain or genre (anime, steampunk, ...). It is the weakest control: scene objects are kept if they fit the theme, and are swapped for a theme-native equivalent only when needed to make sense. Order of precedence when two of them disagree on the same property: `INSTR > STYLE > THEME > original scene`
In practice, with the help of the LLM: `INSTR` edits the scene first, `STYLE` then restyles the result, `THEME` fills in what is still open, and the normal fidelity rules apply to the final scene.
Each control only touches its own scope (e.g. a STYLE never adds or removes a subject; an INSTR subject swap leaves STYLE in force). An empty field is ignored, and if a field appears twice the last one wins. The field names never appear in the output. Quoted text you ask to be visible in the image (e.g. a sign) is kept exactly and is not treated as a control. Since 9.3, we have added a "Neons Style Explorer" (that can be made to generate random styles). When the LLM mode is enabled this will set the STYLE value. Why use them: keep one base scene and vary it without rewriting it. Swap the look (STYLE), the genre (THEME) or the content (INSTR) independently, batch the same scene across several styles, or drive them from wildcards.

nodes.title: Stages
widgets_values:
Upscale note: upscale applies the factor to the width and height (ie if 2x it quadruples the MP: if the original image is 1.5MP, the upscaled image will be 1.5 *2 * 2 = 6MP) Modify parameters note: if not available in the "🔴KSampler Selection", use the arrow in the "Stages" selection to go to the stage nodes and alter its parameters. Images are saved at each Stage, even for bypassed stages. This will enable the use of other workflows and techniques to enhance various stages independently. ### Stage 0: Candidate Selection Enable to select which image to send to further stages. ### Stage 1: Initial Upscaler 3 Options: VOSR2, RTX Super Resolution (requires an Nvidia RTX card) or VSR ### Stage 2: Detailers Uses the `detailer_denoise` and `detailer_steps` from the "🔴KSampler Selection" and the model (and its LoRAs) to find (using Segment Anything Model 3.1) "DetailerX text" and redraw that area. ### Stage 3: Upscaler Resampler Uses the `resampler_denoise` and `resampler_steps` from the "🔴KSampler Selection" and the model (and its LoRAs) to do an upscale (using a `upscale_model`, then an `upscale_factor` applied to width and height -- 2 means 2x height + 2x width so 4 times the MegaPixels). This will increase details but may modify the source image. 💠"USDU" uses "Ultimate SD Upscale".
💠"Image KSampler" pass the source image back through a KSampler.
💠"CustomSampler w/ Detail Daemon" resize then regenerates the image using a `CustomSampler` with the KSampler's Detail Daemon parameters.
💠"Flux USDU" uses a Flux1.D model, a ControlNet and "Ultimate SD Upscale (Custom Sample)" with only the source image to resample the resulting image. Use the arrow to be moved in the workflow to the parameters to adapt them. You must haver enough VRAM to run a Flux1.D model and download the matching ControlNet.
All will enhance details but their speed and enhancements differ. In addition to the steps and denoise, you can vary the `upscale_model`. Some base models/models/image style behave better with one resampler than others, so test with the expected combination before enabling for all generations. This tage is the only stage with its `upscale_factor` configurable in the quick options, the rest requires you to use the arrow (under "opt_connection") to modify the value in the node. ### Stage 4: Final Upscaler Same options as the Initial Upscaler. ## Recommendations For generating illustrations:
💠Use Stage 0, there is no way to fix a bad original image. Keep it on unless you just want to generate a large batch of random/wildcard content and will delete content after generation.
💠Stage 1: Use VOSR2
💠Use Stage 2 and define what you want the two detailers to find and replace (body->face, face->eyes, ...). Use the "Detailer2 Denoise multiplier" for smaller areas (face, eyes, ...) to have it re-generate more details (be cautious not to use too high a value or it will hallucinate details).
💠Stage 3: use USDU (or Flux USDU) with a `4x-UltraMix_Restore` `upscale_model` to avoid introducing too much noise in the resampling using the base model.
💠Stage 4: (optional) Use VOSR2 for a final refinment of lines and illustration details. A note on image size: if you initial image is 1.5MP, a 1.5x VOSR2 (Stage 1) will place it at close to 3.4MP (1.5*1.5*1.5), a 1.5x Upscaler Resampler (Stage 3) at about 7.6MP and a 1.5x final VOSR2 (Stage 4) at about 17MP. "Subgraphs" expose the most common elements to modify, if you want to fine tune USDU for example, simply go into the SubGraph tp alter additional settings.

nodes.title: Order of things
widgets_values:
The output of a mutable node is the input of an "Any Switch", and the last input of that node is the input image of the mutable node. This allows for a bypass in case no mutable node is enabled.

Routing Logic: "Any Switch" out -> Image Saver -> Image Preview -> Reroute -> (Compute Image Size +) Clean VRAM -> VRAM Debug -> Image input for the next stage.


CPipeAny -> VRAM Debug input: This process is to ensure that steps that are expected to be done before another one is done ("wait until ..."). By making it an input in a node that is triggered before the next step, those nodes must finish (show their images or text for example) before the next node in the map can start.

nodes.title: Flux USDU: White lines
widgets_values:
⚠️ Consider lowering the denoise and steps for Anime images. ℹ️ White lines (on art lines) and flat surface artifacts are sign of "over-exposure" to the high-frequency detail commands when applied to an anime aesthetic. Potential values:
**Denoise: 0.20** (or below): Dropping prevents the model from "redrawing" flat surfaces and lines.
**Steps: 15** (or below)
